title: Escalation journal — standby notes (Diego)
body:
Purpose: personal scratchpad for war‑room readiness and quick handoffs. Put this on my phone as single-page cheat. Not a polished ops doc — notes to self and action tracker.

Context: Customer B reported repeated timeouts on hosted inference for high-concurrency inference group (batching spikes during overnight import). Affects dedicated + hosted fallback path. SLOs: 95th latency < 350ms, customer getting 2–3s spikes. Suspected causes: jitter from autoscaler, KV cache churn, and occasional model fallback to quantized variant.

Agenda (quick call prep)
- 0:00–0:03: short context + impact (who is impacted: ingest jobs, UI refreshers)
- 0:03–0:08: last 30m timeline and observable anomalies (p95, p99, error types)
- 0:08–0:13: decide immediate mitigation (route to dedicated pool? throttle? rollback rollout?)
- 0:13–0:18: assign owners for data collection + short-term fixes
- 0:18–0:25: comms plan + next check-in cadence (30m / 1h)

Immediate checklist (first 15m)
- [ ] Share p95/p99 from Redwood Console (Tom) — ask for 15/5/1m windows
- [ ] Check autoscaler events for dedicated pool (Lina)
- [ ] Confirm whether fallback to quantized model occurred (grep model_variant in logs) (me)
- [ ] Temporarily disable rollout for model v2026-03 if active (SRE on call)
- [ ] Notify CS lead and customer PM: brief note + ETA (me)

Data to capture (urgent)
- latency time series (1m resolution): frontend->api->runtime token times
- autoscaler scale events + GPU allocation timeline
- serving-runtime logs: kernel selection warnings, cache evictions, OOM traces
- sample request/response ids matching spikes (trace ids)
- any recent config changes (rollouts, batching config, quantization overrides) — check PR list in last 48h

Runbook snippets I care about (quick links)
- fallback routing: /ops/runbook/fallback-routing (read only the decision matrix)
- autoscaler troubleshooting: /ops/runbook/autoscaler
- model rollout rollback steps: short script: rollback.sh --env=prod --model=vX -> confirm no migrate needed

Mitigation options (tradeoffs)
- Route affected customer to dedicated reserved pool: +predictable, -time to move (10–20m), requires SRE coordination
- Apply temporary concurrency cap per API key: fast, low lift, may degrade throughput for customer ingest
- Force-model-pin to non-quantized variant: stops fallback-induced jitter but increases token cost
- Increase autoscaler aggressiveness (lower cooldown): maybe reduces p99 but risks overprovisioning cost

Communication snippets (copy for Slack / email)
- Slack to #cust-B-urgent: "We see elevated latency for your ingest jobs; investigating root cause. Short-term mitigation in progress. Next update in 30m. — Diego"
- If routing to dedicated: "We are routing your traffic to a reserved pool to stabilize latency while we investigate. No action required from your side. Estimated completion: 20–30m."

Hand-off table (post-call)
- Data collection: Tom Brooks — collect p95/p99, sample traces, autoscaler events — due: +30m
- Short-term mitigation: Lina Chen / SRE-on-call — implement concurrency cap + pin model — due: +20m
- Customer comms: Diego — send initial and follow-up messages — due: immediate / +30m
- Postmortem owner: (TBD on resolution) — create incident page, link logs and timeline — due: within 24h

Open questions / notes to self
- Are there any infra maintenance windows overlapping? check infra calendar (might explain planar GPU maintenance)
- Confirm whether private deployment customers saw same issue (if not, might be routing rule specific to hosted)
- If fallback detected, what triggered it? KV cache miss vs model health signal? Find the alert rule that triggers fallback.
- Save the sequence of client IDs affected for later sampling (ask Tom for top-10 request ids).

Post-meeting quick actions (what I will do immediately)
- DM Lina + SRE-on-call with checklist and ask for ETA
- Drop link to this scratchpad in the warroom thread with short TL;DR
- Copy initial comm to customer PM and legal if escalates to SLA credits

Triage heuristics (personal)
- If p99 > 2s and >15% of requests in window -> escalate priority to P0 and route to dedicated
- If errors are 5xx and sudden spike -> prioritize runtime logs and kernel warnings
- If only single region affected -> consider regional routing fallback first

Templates / boilerplate to reuse (short snippets)
- "Short update: we observed elevated latency for customer B between 10:12–10:47 UTC. We've applied a temporary concurrency cap and are routing traffic to a reserved pool. Next update in 30m."
- Postmortem outline: timeline, impact (users, tokens), root cause analysis, mitigations, follow-up actions + owners, prevention plan

Personal reminders (handy)
- Keep the call <30m if possible. We rarely need more than quick mitigation + data capture for these events.
- Save the final decision in a one-sentence summary at top of incident page (for legal / exec).
- After resolution: schedule a 30m deep-dive with serving-runtime if kernel warnings show up.

Log of quick calls (for this incident)
- 2026-03-10 09:54 UTC: triage call started (me, Lina, Tom, SRE-on-call)
- 2026-03-10 10:02 UTC: applied concurrency cap -> p95 improved from 1.2s to 380ms for test window
- 2026-03-10 10:15 UTC: routed traffic to reserved pool -> p99 stabilized under 600ms

Final notes (sticky)
- If this repeats within 48h, we should consider a hotspot analysis on sequence-length distribution and batching windows. Could be a workload pattern mismatch with batching heuristics.
- Add follow-up item: request model profiling snapshot for the customer's top-20 prompts (to check KV cache warmup)

-- end of scratchpad (save to warroom thread as working note)
